architecture.title: One harness, two deployment models — identical input, independent policy
architecture.caption: The shared runner serializes each row's state ONCE and sends the byte-identical string to Jev (hosted) and Laya (local). A no-truncation preflight blocks unfair Laya input; results, hashes and failures land in a new run folder. Neither model's answer is ever an action.

lanes.label: Evidence — a new folder per run

nodes.label: results.jsonl + summary.json
nodes.sub: failures kept · hashes · no raw state

sequence.title: Lab 10 — verify, plan, then (and only then) spend
sequence.caption: Labs 01 and 02 cost nothing and prove the harness is honest; lab 03 is the only billed step (~28 calls, ≈ $0.001); lab 04 probes negation because averages hide it.

steps.label: Laya side is optional: same command + --live-laya

charts.title: Published typed-decisions results — as published on the Laya model card, NOT reproduced
charts.caption: Source: huggingface.co/convaiinnovations/laya-typed-decisions. The card states Jev was not run by that project and prompts/sample sizes differ — so this is not a head-to-head result. Higher accuracy (Laya) and better calibration (Jev, lower ECE) point in different directions.

charts.title: Our Jev-only smoke run — labeled decisions per question
charts.caption: Measured by labs/lab03_jev_only_benchmark.py (jev-1.13.0, 28 rows, 2026-09-27). With 1–11 labels per question, one disagreement moves accuracy by 9–100 points — a smoke test shows the plumbing, not the quality.
